Modern Iraq was established as an independent country on **October 3, 1932**, following World War I and gaining full sovereignty after British administration ended. The Kingdom of Iraq was proclaimed in 1931, and independence was formally recognized in 1932.

While Iraq has ancient roots as one of the world's earliest civilizations (with settlements dating back thousands of years), the modern nation-state emerged in the early 20th century after the dissolution of the Ottoman Empire.

**Answer: Iraq was established as an independent country on October 3, 1932.**
